name: Chromatic Abbest
summary: The supercharged form of the Abbest, the robed caster enemy found across the early areas. Like every Chromatic variant it is a tougher encounter with a matching reward tier rather than a new move set, so the answer is the same element that works on the base enemy.

name: Chromatic Bourgeon
summary: The Chromatic form of the Bourgeon, the flower-bodied Nevron that guards the Flying Waters approach. Fire is the reliable answer and it stays the reliable answer on the variant.

name: Chromatic Bruler
summary: A Chromatic Bruler. The base enemy is a straightforward melee Nevron with a Lightning weakness, and the variant keeps that profile while hitting considerably harder.

name: Chromatic Chalier
summary: The Chromatic form of Chalier. Light is the weakness and Dark is resisted, which makes it one of the fights where a Dark-heavy Sciel build is actively worse than a Light line.

name: Chromatic Danseuse
weak: Fire in Ice Stance, Ice in Fire Stance
absorbs: Fire in Fire Stance, Ice in Ice Stance
summary: The Chromatic Danseuse keeps the base enemy's stance mechanic: it absorbs whichever element it is currently in and is weak to the opposite. Read the stance before you commit a turn, exactly as with Stalact.

name: Chromatic Gault
summary: A Chromatic Gault. Three elements matter here - Fire lands, Ice and Lightning are resisted, and Earth is absorbed, so an Earth-based skill is a net loss on this fight.

name: Chromatic Greatsword Cultist
summary: The Chromatic form of the Greatsword Cultist. Dark is the only element that lands cleanly, and the variant drops a Dark-leaning weapon for Sciel, so the fight pays for the correct build twice over.

name: Chromatic Hexga
summary: A Chromatic Hexga. Ice is the weakness and Fire is resisted, so the obvious guess from its icy appearance is correct and the obvious counter-guess from its apparent element is not.

name: Chromatic Jar
locations: The Continent, west of Old Lumiere
summary: A Chromatic Jar, and unusually generous on weaknesses: four of the six elements land, while Physical is the resisted one. Physical-only parties are the wrong pick here for once.

name: Chromatic Lancelier
summary: The Chromatic Lancelier is one of the earliest optional bosses in the game and a common first death for players who wander into it under-levelled. Ice is the answer; the level gap is the real problem.

name: Chromatic Luster
summary: A Chromatic Luster. Lightning is the weakness, and the variant drops a Dark-element weapon, which makes it worth doing even though the drop element does not match the fight's own weakness.

name: Chromatic Orphelin
summary: The Chromatic Orphelin. Earth is the one element that lands, and clearing it is the route to Kralim, one of Lune's stronger Lightning focuses - so the reward does not match the weakness.

name: Chromatic Ramasseur
summary: A Chromatic Ramasseur. Light lands and Dark is resisted, the same pairing as Chalier and Troubadour, so a Light-focused party covers several of the Act 2 Chromatic fights at once.

name: Chromatic Troubadour
summary: The Chromatic Troubadour drops Troubadim, a Physical focus for Lune, despite being weak to Light. Its attack repertoire is built around disruption rather than raw damage.

name: Alicia
summary: Alicia is an Act 3 optional boss in The Reacher, reached through Maelle's relationship questline rather than through the map. Access is gated behind relationship level, which is why many players finish the game without ever meeting her.

name: Simon
summary: Simon, the Divergent Star, is the hardest fight in the base game and the gate to Simoso, one of the strongest weapons for Verso. He has no elemental weakness, so the fight is decided entirely by build quality and parry timing.

name: Bertrand Big Hands
summary: An Arena opponent in the Hidden Gestral Arena tournament. Arena fights are 1v1, so party synergy cannot cover for a bad matchup - the whole result is your own parry timing and single-target damage.

name: Dominique Giant Feet
summary: An Arena opponent in the Hidden Gestral Arena, part of the same tournament chain as Matthieu the Colossus and Julien Tiny Head. Like the rest of the set it is a 1v1 skill check with no elemental puzzle.

name: Dominique Tiny Feet
summary: The smaller half of the Dominique pair in the Hidden Gestral Arena tournament. Arena rules apply: bring your most self-sufficient character, not your best support.

name: Jovial Moissonneuse
summary: One of the three masks connected to the Axon in Visages, and one of the three Vale bosses that feed Mask Keeper's extra abilities. Defeating it before the main fight directly removes one of those buffs.

name: Seething Boucheclier
summary: A second mask connected to the Visages Axon, encountered in the Visages area. Killing it before Mask Keeper is one of the three pre-fight reductions that measurably lower the difficulty of the second stage.

name: Sorrowful Chapelier
summary: The third mask attached to the Visages Axon. It shares the Fire and Dark weakness of the other two Vale bosses, so the same party clears all three without rebuilding.

name: Clair Obscur
summary: The Clair Obscur is a boss form of the paired Clair and Obscur enemies, found in the Tainted Lumiere area of The Monolith. It shares their silhouette but carries far more health and a heavier attack set, and it drops Dreameso.

name: White-Haired Man
summary: The White-Haired Man is the first appearance of the character you later fight properly as Renoir. This encounter is the introduction to his move set and the reason the later fights feel familiar rather than new.

name: Gargant
summary: Gargant is a rock-bodied boss assembled from stones marked with golden veins, encountered in Frozen Hearts and again later in The Monolith. Beating it in Frozen Hearts is how you obtain Snowim.

name: Jar
summary: The Jar is an early optional boss with an unusually wide weakness list: four elements land, while Physical is the resisted one. Its Chromatic form keeps the same profile.

name: Bourgeon
locations: Flying Waters, Stone Wave Cliffs, The Continent
summary: Bourgeon is a recurring flower-bodied Nevron boss that appears in three separate places across Act 1 and Act 2. Fire is the answer every time, and defeating the Flying Waters instance is how you obtain Abysseram.

name: Mime
locations: Lumiere, Spring Meadows, Flying Waters, and six later areas
summary: Mimes are a recurring optional encounter scattered across at least nine areas of the game, from the prologue through the postgame. They have no elemental weakness or resistance at all, which makes them pure execution fights and the reason they are excluded from every weakness chart.
